title: WSC+: Enhancing The Winograd Schema Challenge Using Tree-of-Experts
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the model's ability to detect stereotypes and biases in ambiguous religious contexts. Specifically, it tested whether a model would default to a stereotyped answer or correctly identify that a sentence lacks sufficient information to resolve a pronoun when religious groups are mentioned.
findings: LLMs can bypass their safety mechanisms with nuanced prompts to generate sentences containing religious stereotypes. When evaluating these 'offensive' sentences, models often correctly choose the 'neither' option not because they recognize the ambiguity, but because their safety filters are triggered by the controversial nature of the content. For example, prompting Claude2 for racially offensive content led it to produce biases across other dimensions, including religion.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. 2021. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models. In Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, pages 298–306.
